cards.explanation: The answer is whirlwinds. The prophet says the invader comes "Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, an invader comes from the desert, from a land of terror." (Isaiah 21:1) Picture a pan of cookies getting swept off the counter by one big spin. That's the kind of force the verse puts in front of us, friends.

The answer is go up and lay siege. The vision says, "Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media!" (Isaiah 21:2) Elam and Media are two nations, and they're the ones getting the orders here, bakers. A siege means surrounding a city and pressing in on it.

The answer is False. The prophet says, "Therefore my body is filled with anguish." (Isaiah 21:3) He's bewildered by what he hears and dismayed by what he sees. Nobody's kicking back with a cold drink after a vision like that, friends.

The answer is horror. The prophet says, "The twilight I desired has turned to horror." (Isaiah 21:4) Twilight is the soft end of the day, the part you'd want to enjoy. His went the other way, and I'd say that's a hard turn, friends.

The answer is oil the shields. The call says, "Rise up, O princes, oil the shields!" (Isaiah 21:5) It comes right in the middle of the table, the carpet, the eating and the drinking. I think that's a loud way to say the party is about to get interrupted, bakers.

The answer is chariots and riders. The Lord says the lookout will see "…chariots with teams of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels…" (Isaiah 21:7) That's a lot of different riders to keep track of, friends. The lookout has plenty to keep his eyes on.
The answer is True. The Lord says, "…he must be alert, fully alert." (Isaiah 21:7) That's the whole job, friends. Half alert won't do it, and neither will a nap.

The answer is fallen, and it's said twice. "Fallen, fallen is Babylon!" (Isaiah 21:9) Saying it twice makes it ring like a bell, bakers. The lookout watched day after day and night after night, and this was the news that came.

The answer is True. The voice says, "All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!" (Isaiah 21:9) Those images couldn't even stay in one piece, friends. That's a hard line to hear about Babylon.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts. The prophet says, "…I tell you what I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel." (Isaiah 21:10) He gives the source right there, by name, friends. He's speaking to his people, who he calls "…crushed on the threshing floor…"
